sentences: Three-edge-colorability asks whether the edges of a graph can receive three colors with different colors on every pair meeting at a vertex.
The selected question asks for the computational complexity of this decision problem on planar graphs.
The source studies a sufficient route through augmentation to a planar cubic bridgeless supergraph, where three-edge-colorability follows from the Four-Color Theorem.
It also discusses a conjectured characterization for two-connected planar graphs of maximum degree three.
A full classification would determine whether the remaining planar cases admit an efficient coloring test or conceal an NP-hard obstruction.
